# Component Catalogue

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen/components.js from packages/ui/src. Do not edit; run `npm run gen:components`. -->

Every shared component of both apps, read from its header and its props in `packages/ui/src`.
Features import from `@mycity/ui` only, and never build their own copy of anything listed here.

**Need something that is not here?** Add it to the package, never inside a feature:

```bash
npm run new:component -- --name StatusPill --group Display
```

That writes the component with its header, a test and a gallery page, exports it from its group,
and regenerates this file. Fill the header, build it, run `npm -w @mycity/ui test` and see it in
`npm run gallery`. `scripts/check/components.js` fails a stale catalogue, a component without a full
header, test or gallery page, and a feature that re-creates or shadows a component listed here.

## Foundations

### Icon

One Lucide glyph by its short name, drawn in the current text colour.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Beside a word on a button, a nav item, a KPI card or a status line; alone only for well known actions inside an IconButton. |
| Avoid | Emoji, another icon set or an inline SVG; an icon alone with no IconButton or label around it. |
| Phone | The same glyph; the bottom bar and the More tiles show it at 20 or 24 px. |
| Accessibility | Decorative (aria-hidden) unless given a label, which makes it role="img" with that name. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Icon` |
| Import | `import { Icon } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/icons/Icon.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/icons/Icon.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/icons/Icon.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Icon`) |

**Icon** props (`IconProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `IconName` | yes | The glyph, by its short name. |
| `size` | `"s" \| "m" \| "l"` |  | `s` 16 px inline (the default), `m` 20 px navigation, `l` 24 px bottom bar and tiles. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes: a token text colour, or a size class to override the box. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Gives the icon a name for assistive technology; without it the icon is decorative. |

```tsx
<Icon name="clock" />
<Icon name="alert" size="m" label="Late" />
```

## Actions

### ActionGroup

Buttons that wait for each other: while one is working, the others in the group dim and ignore presses until it finishes.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Around buttons that act on the same thing and must not race: Approve and Reject on a request row, Retire and Edit on a record. Modals, forms, form footers, card headers, page headers and shell notices are groups already. |
| Avoid | Around a whole page or list (one slow request would hold every row); around a single button (it already ignores a second press); for layout (it draws no element). |
| Phone | The same: the waiting buttons dim and keep their 44 px targets. |
| Accessibility | Draws no element of its own. A busy button says aria-busy; the waiting ones say aria-disabled, so a screen reader hears them as unavailable while they stay focusable. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `ActionGroup` |
| Import | `import { ActionGroup } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/actions/ActionGroup.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/actions/ActionGroup.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/actions/ActionGroup.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/ActionGroup`) |

**ActionGroup** props (`ActionGroupProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The buttons, laid out by the caller: the group adds behaviour, not markup. |

```tsx
<ActionGroup><Button onClick={reject}>Reject</Button><Button variant="primary" onClick={approve}>Approve</Button></ActionGroup>
```

### Button

The pill button: default, primary (the yellow one), ghost and danger, with an optional icon either side; busy from the press until the work it starts is done.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Every action a person takes: Create Rule, Clock In, Export. Hand it the work (onClick={save}, an async handler) and it spins and ignores a second press until the work settles. A link that looks like a button passes asChild with an <a>. |
| Avoid | A second primary on one surface (one yellow button per surface); a bare icon (use IconButton); the sign in or clock in call to action (use BigButton); throwing the work away (onClick={() => void save()}: the lint refuses it, F26). |
| Phone | At least 44 px tall; a footer stretches the primary to full width at the bottom. Busy keeps its size and colour, so nothing beside it moves. |
| Accessibility | A native button (type="button" unless set). Busy, it keeps its colour, softens, shows a spinner and says aria-busy; it and the buttons in its ActionGroup ignore presses but stay focusable and named (aria-disabled, never disabled). Verb Noun labels, Title Case. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Button`, `IconButton`, `BigButton` |
| Import | `import { Button, IconButton, BigButton } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/actions/Button.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/actions/Button.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/actions/Button.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Button`) |

**Button** props (`ButtonProps`, extends `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "onClick">`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | `"default" \| "primary" \| "ghost" \| "danger"` |  | `primary` is the yellow one, one per surface; `danger` is for destructive actions, confirmed in a dialog. |
| `icon` | `IconName` |  | A glyph before the label. |
| `iconRight` | `IconName` |  | A glyph after the label (a chevron for "View All"). |
| `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` |  | `md` follows the density (36 or 40 px); `sm` is 28 px on desktop. Both are 44 px on a phone. |
| `block` | `boolean` |  | Fills the width: the call to action at the foot of a form or page. |
| `onClick` | `PressHandler<MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>>` |  | The press. Return the work (onClick={save}, or an async handler) and the button is busy from the press until it settles: a spinner, presses ignored, and its ActionGroup waiting with it. |
| `busy` | `boolean` |  | Busy by the caller's own measure (a mutation's pending), for work the press does not return. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | Renders the single child element (an <a>, a router Link) with the button's look instead of a <button>. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The label: Verb Noun, Title Case, at most 3 words. |

**IconButton** props (`IconButtonProps`, extends `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "children" | "aria-label" | "onClick">`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `IconName` | yes | The glyph. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | What the button does, in words: its accessible name and its tooltip. Required. |
| `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` |  | `md` follows the density; `sm` is 32 px on desktop. Both are 44 px on a phone. |
| `dot` | `boolean` |  | A small red dot for something new (the bell). |
| `onClick` | `PressHandler<MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>>` |  | The press. Return the work and the glyph turns to a spinner until it settles, presses ignored meanwhile. |
| `busy` | `boolean` |  | Busy by the caller's own measure, for work the press does not return. |

**BigButton** props (`BigButtonProps`, extends `Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "onClick">`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `IconName` |  | A glyph after the label. |
| `onClick` | `PressHandler<MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>>` |  | The press. Return the work and it spins until the work settles, presses ignored meanwhile. |
| `busy` | `boolean` |  | Busy by the caller's own measure (a sign-in form's submit). |

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" icon="plus">New Rule</Button>
<Button variant="primary" onClick={save}>Save Worksite</Button>
<Button variant="ghost" iconRight="right">View All</Button>
```

## Layout

### Card

The raised panel every section sits in, with an optional title row (CardHeader) and one Details row at its foot.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A section of a page: a KPI group, a record's fields, a list, a chart. One idea per card. |
| Avoid | Cards inside cards; an explainer card (a title starting How, Why or What is tier 3 and never reaches a screen); a list on a phone (a card list comes from DataView). |
| Phone | Full width with the same padding; the actions in CardHeader keep their 44 px targets and wrap under the title when there is no room. |
| Accessibility | A plain container. CardHeader's title is a heading (h2 unless set: a card is a section of the page under its h1) marked data-ui="title"; give a card that is itself clickable a role and a name, or better, put a Button inside it. CardHeader's actions wait for each other while one is working (F26). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Card`, `CardHeader` |
| Import | `import { Card, CardHeader } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/layout/Card.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/layout/Card.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/layout/Card.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Card`) |

**Card** props (`CardProps`, extends `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pad` | `boolean` |  | Inner padding (the default). `false` lets a table, a list or an image run to the card's edges. |
| `as` | `"div" \| "section" \| "article"` |  | The element: `section` when the card has its own heading in a long page, `article` for one record. |
| `details` | `ReactNode` |  | The one Details row at the foot of the card (a Details from |
| `urgency` | `"normal" \| "important" \| "urgent"` |  | A notice's level: an amber edge when important; a red edge that pulses slowly when urgent (steady when motion is off). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The card's content. |

**CardHeader** props (`CardHeaderProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | The card's title: a noun phrase of at most 4 words, Title Case (Leave Requests). |
| `help` | `ReactNode` |  | Support text behind the title, at most 35 words: the title becomes a HelpTerm. |
| `record` | `boolean` |  | The title is record content (a person's name, a document number), not interface copy: the copy gates skip it. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | What sits at the right: a small button, a menu, a pill or a count. |
| `right` | `ReactNode` |  | The merged name for `actions`; kept so screens move by an import change. |
| `level` | `2 \| 3 \| 4` |  | The heading level; h2 (a section of the page) unless the card sits inside another section, where it is h3. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Anything else after the title (a pill, a count). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<Card><CardHeader title="Leave Requests" actions={<Button size="sm">View All</Button>} />...</Card>
<Card details={<Details>...</Details>}>...</Card>
<Card urgency="urgent">...</Card>
```

### Grid

The page grid: 2, 3 or 4 equal columns, or a wide and a narrow column, collapsing to one column on a phone.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Laying out cards on a page: KPI tiles (4), two cards side by side (2), a list beside its detail ("1.4/1"). On desktop two columns side by side each stop at the window's height and scroll on their own, as the mailbox's panes do; `scroll={false}` lets them grow with the page. |
| Avoid | Laying out controls inside a card (use Stack or Inline); a table's columns. |
| Phone | One column, except `phoneCols={2}` (or the merged "4m2"), which keeps KPI tiles two to a row. Nothing scrolls on its own. |
| Accessibility | A plain container; reading order is the source order at every width. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Grid` |
| Import | `import { Grid } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/layout/Grid.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/layout/Grid.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/layout/Grid.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Grid`) |

**Grid** props (`GridProps`, extends `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cols` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| "4m2" \| "1.4/1" \| "1/1.5"` | yes | How many columns on desktop; see GridCols. |
| `phoneCols` | `1 \| 2` |  | Columns on a phone: 1 (the default) or 2 (KPI tiles). |
| `gap` | `"sm" \| "md"` |  | Space between cells: `md` 12 px (the default) or `sm` 8 px. |
| `flush` | `boolean` |  | Drop the 12 px space under the grid (the merged grids carry it so blocks stack apart). |
| `scroll` | `boolean` |  | Two columns side by side scroll on their own on desktop (the default); `false` lets them grow with the page. |

```tsx
<Grid cols={4} phoneCols={2}>{kpis}</Grid>
<Grid cols="1.4/1"><Card /><Card /></Grid>
```

### PageHeader

A page's title, its one-line subtitle (desktop only) and the page's actions.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Once, at the top of every screen. |
| Avoid | A second title further down (use CardHeader); a subtitle that explains how the page works (tier 3); more than one primary action. |
| Phone | The subtitle is not shown (FRONTEND_GUIDE §7: less text); the actions wrap under the title with 44 px targets. |
| Accessibility | The title is the page's only h1 (data-ui="page-title"); the subtitle is a paragraph (data-ui="page-subtitle"). Title at most 3 words, subtitle at most 8. The actions wait for each other while one is working (F26). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `PageHeader` |
| Import | `import { PageHeader } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/layout/PageHeader.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/layout/PageHeader.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/layout/PageHeader.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/PageHeader`) |

**PageHeader** props (`PageHeaderProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes | The page's name, at most 3 words, Title Case (My Attendance). Something beside it, such as a Pill, may follow as children of the title. |
| `help` | `ReactNode` |  | Support text behind the title (a HelpTerm on it), at most 35 words. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` |  | One line under the title, at most 8 words; desktop only. |
| `sub` | `ReactNode` |  | The merged name for `subtitle`; kept so screens move by an import change. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | The page's actions, at the right on desktop: at most one primary Button. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Anything between the title and the actions (a filter, a period switch). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<PageHeader title="My Leave" subtitle="2026 entitlement" actions={<Button variant="primary" icon="plus">Request Leave</Button>} />
```

### PhoneOnly

Shows its content on a phone only; DesktopOnly shows it on a desktop only. What each shell leaves out is decided per screen.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | The pieces a feature guide's §10 lists for one shell: icon cards on a phone, a chart or an extra column on desktop. |
| Avoid | Hiding something by accident of width; the whole page twice (each shell is a layout, not a copy); a table on a phone (DataView draws the card list). |
| Phone | PhoneOnly renders at 760 px and below, DesktopOnly at 761 px and above, the same width as useIsPhone() and the gates. |
| Accessibility | Hidden content is display:none, so it is out of the accessibility tree too. With `unmount` the hidden side is not rendered at all. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `PhoneOnly`, `DesktopOnly` |
| Import | `import { PhoneOnly, DesktopOnly } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/layout/PhoneOnly.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/layout/PhoneOnly.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/layout/PhoneOnly.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/PhoneOnly`) |

**PhoneOnly** props (`PhoneOnlyProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What only a phone shows. |
| `unmount` | `boolean` |  | Do not render it at all on desktop (for something heavy); by default it is rendered and hidden with CSS, so there is no flash on first paint. |
| `as` | `"div" \| "span"` |  | `span` inside a line of text; `div` otherwise. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only. |

**DesktopOnly** props (`DesktopOnlyProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What only a desktop shows. |
| `unmount` | `boolean` |  | Do not render it at all on a phone (for something heavy, such as a chart); by default it is rendered and hidden with CSS. |
| `as` | `"div" \| "span"` |  | `span` inside a line of text; `div` otherwise. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only. |

```tsx
<PhoneOnly><IconCards>...</IconCards></PhoneOnly>
<DesktopOnly unmount><AreaChart /></DesktopOnly>
```

### SplitPanes

A list beside the record it opens, with a divider the person can drag; on a phone the list fills the screen and the record covers it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A screen read one record at a time out of a list: the mailbox, chat, a day's punches. |
| Avoid | A page of sections (use Grid); a list and a detail that fit side by side at a fixed width (use Grid "1.4/1"); three panes a person drags independently. |
| Phone | There are no panes: the list fills the screen and an open record covers it, above the shell, with the safe area kept clear. |
| Accessibility | The divider is a real separator with its width as its value, and the arrow keys move it, so the panes can be resized without a pointer. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `SplitPanes` |
| Import | `import { SplitPanes } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/layout/SplitPanes.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/layout/SplitPanes.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/layout/SplitPanes.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/SplitPanes`) |

**SplitPanes** props (`SplitPanesProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `split` | `SplitState` | yes | The width and the drag, from `useSplitPanes`. |
| `list` | `ReactNode` | yes | The list, which fills the screen on a phone. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` | yes | The record in view, which covers the list on a phone. |
| `aside` | `ReactNode` |  | A third pane at the right on desktop, 300 px wide (a channel's own information). |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | A record is open: on a phone it covers the list. |
| `minHeight` | `"sm" \| "md"` |  | The panes' least height; `md` unless a screen wants more. |
| `scrolls` | `boolean` |  | The open record scrolls as one, rather than its own parts scrolling (the mailbox reads this way). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
const split = useSplitPanes("mailbox", 320);
<SplitPanes split={split} open={open} list={list} detail={reader} />
```

### Stack

A vertical run of blocks with an even gap; Inline is the horizontal run that wraps.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Spacing blocks inside a card or a sheet (Stack), and a row of pills, buttons or figures (Inline), on the token spacing scale. |
| Avoid | Page columns (use Grid); hand-written margins between siblings. |
| Phone | The same; Inline wraps rather than scrolling the page sideways. |
| Accessibility | A plain container (a list when as="ul"); reading order is the source order. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Stack`, `Inline` |
| Import | `import { Stack, Inline } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/layout/Stack.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/layout/Stack.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/layout/Stack.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Stack`) |

**Stack** props (`StackProps`, extends `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap` | `0 \| 1 \| 1.5 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` |  | Space between the blocks; 3 (12 px) unless set. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` |  | Cross-axis alignment: stretch (the default) fills the width. |
| `as` | `"div" \| "section" \| "ul" \| "ol"` |  | The element: a div, or a list when the blocks are list items. |

**Inline** props (`InlineProps`, extends `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap` | `0 \| 1 \| 1.5 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` |  | Space between the items; 2 (8 px) unless set. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "stretch" \| "baseline"` |  | Cross-axis alignment: center unless set. |
| `justify` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end" \| "between"` |  | Main-axis distribution: start unless set; `between` pushes the last item to the end. |
| `nowrap` | `boolean` |  | Keep everything on one line (it then truncates rather than wrapping). |
| `as` | `"div" \| "span" \| "ul" \| "ol"` |  | The element: a div, or a list when the items are list items. |

```tsx
<Stack gap={3}><KeyValue items={rows} /><Banner tone="info">Payroll closes Friday</Banner></Stack>
<Inline gap={2}><Pill tone="ok">Approved</Pill><Pill>Annual Leave</Pill></Inline>
```

## Display

### Accordion

Questions and their answers, each closed until it is opened.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A set of FAQs (the Knowledge Hub), a policy's clauses, a long list of named notes a person reads one of. |
| Avoid | Support text on a screen (use HelpTerm or Details); hiding something a person needs to act (that is tier 1, and belongs open); one item on its own (use Details). |
| Phone | The same rows, each at least 44 px tall, opening in place rather than in a sheet. |
| Accessibility | Native disclosures, so the keyboard and screen readers work without any script; the + marker is decorative. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Accordion` |
| Import | `import { Accordion } from "@mycity/ui";` |

### Avatar

A person's photo, or their initials in a round chip when there is none, with an optional presence dot; Who is the avatar with the name and a second line.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Beside a person's name in a list, a card, a chat, a record header (Who for the name and role together). |
| Avoid | An organisation's logo; a stack of avatars with no names and no label; a decorative picture. |
| Phone | The same sizes; `md` and up in lists so the row reaches 44 px. |
| Accessibility | Decorative (hidden) beside a visible name. Standalone, pass label (the person's name): it becomes an image with that name, and its presence is said too. Who marks the name as content. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Avatar`, `Who` |
| Import | `import { Avatar, Who } from "@mycity/ui";` |

One line across a page or a card in a status tone, with an icon and at most one action.

| Use | Something the person must know or do now: a policy to acknowledge, a run that is locked, a device limit reached. |

| Phone | Full width; the action drops under the line, 44 px tall. |
| Accessibility | A status region, or an alert for tone="err", so it is announced when it appears. The icon is decorative; the words carry the meaning, at most 20. |

### CityShowcase

The sign-in screen's picture: photographs of eight cities at dusk taking turns, drifting slowly under a film grain and rising points of light, each with its ticking clock, and the sign-in form in a panel of smoked glass.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | The staff sign-in screen only: `full` fills the screen on desktop with the form beside the city, `phone` fills a phone's screen with the form under it. |

| Phone | variant="phone": the portrait photograph fills the screen and drifts, with the brand and a glass clock at the top, the city and its turn below them, and the form in the smoked glass panel at the foot. |
| Accessibility | The photographs, drawings, grain and lights are decorative (empty alt, aria-hidden). The cities are a group of buttons, each naming the city and its time, the shown one marked aria-current. Turning pauses while the pointer or focus is on them; under reduced motion nothing moves and the cities stop turning. The glass panel takes the dark theme's colours (data-theme="dark"), so its text keeps AA over any photograph. |
| Status | beta |

| `variant` | `"full" \| "phone"` |  | `full` fills its parent, with the clock and the city buttons at the foot; `phone` fills a phone's screen, the picture at the top. |

| `start` | `CityKey` |  | The first city shown. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What sits at the top over the picture: the brand, and on `full` a headline. |
| `aside` | `ReactNode` |  | The sign-in form, set in the smoked glass panel: `full` at the right over the picture, centred, with the clock and the cities clear of it; `phone` at the foot, under the city. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (height, the grid cell); the look is the component's own. |

```tsx
<CityShowcase variant="phone" aside={<SignInForm />}><Brand tone="on-dark" /></CityShowcase>
```

|---|---|

| Accessibility | The title is a heading (data-ui="title"): h2 as its own card on a page, h3 when bare inside a card or a sheet; at most 4 words; the line (data-ui="empty-text") at most 8. The drawing is decorative. |

### ItemChip

A rounded chip naming one item (a module in a role), tapped to open it, with small marks after the name.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A wrapped set of items a person opens one at a time: the modules a role reaches at one level, each opening its detail, with letters after the name for what applies to it. |
| Avoid | Narrowing a list (use Chips); a status on a record (use Pill); records with more to say than a name (use TapList, or DataView for a server list). |
| Phone | The name is a 44 px tap target; a row of chips wraps onto new lines and never scrolls the page sideways. Marks that are help terms open their sheet on a tap. |
| Accessibility | With onSelect the name is a button that opens a dialog (aria-haspopup), with aria-current on the item open now; pass `label` when the name alone is not enough. The marks sit beside the button, never inside it, so each can be a control of its own. The name is marked as content (data-copy). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `ItemChip` |
| Import | `import { ItemChip } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/display/ItemChip.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/display/ItemChip.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/display/ItemChip.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/ItemChip`) |

**ItemChip** props (`ItemChipProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes | The item's name as the screen shows it; record content, not interface copy. |
| `onSelect` | `() => void` |  | Opens the item. Without it the chip is a plain label, not a control. |
| `marks` | `ReactNode` |  | Small marks after the name, such as letters behind help terms; they sit outside the chip's button so each can be a control of its own. |
| `selected` | `boolean` |  | The item open now: drawn in the accent. |
| `muted` | `boolean` |  | An item that is off (no access): drawn muted. |
| `label` | `string` |  | The button's accessible name when the visible name is not enough ("Payroll, View, Team"). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<ItemChip onSelect={() => open("payroll")} label="Payroll, View, Team">Payroll</ItemChip>
<ItemChip selected onSelect={() => open("people")} marks={<HelpTerm help={teamHelp}>T</HelpTerm>}>People</ItemChip>
```

### KpiCard

One figure a person acts on: its title, the number, and a short trend line; with `onOpen` it becomes the way into the records behind it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A role's figures at the top of Home, a record's own counts, a module's four tiles above its list. |
| Avoid | A sentence about the number (put it behind the help); a tile for a figure nobody acts on; more than four on one row. |
| Phone | Two to a row in a KpiGrid, with the number a size smaller; opening one shows its records as a bottom sheet. |
| Accessibility | A tile that opens something is a button named by its title and value, with the chevron decorative; its help is an InfoButton beside the button, never a focusable term inside it; the trend's direction is a word, never colour alone. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `KpiCard` |
| Import | `import { KpiCard } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/display/KpiCard.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/display/KpiCard.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/display/KpiCard.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/KpiCard`) |

**KpiCard** props (`KpiCardProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes | The figure's name, Title Case, at most 4 words (Clocked In Today). |
| `value` | `ReactNode` | yes | The figure itself: a count, a Money, a fraction ("22 of 25"). |
| `tone` | `StatusTone` |  | The number's tone, when the figure itself is good or bad news. |
| `caption` | `ReactNode` |  | The line under the number, at most 5 words (4 overdue, 3 more than last month). |
| `trend` | `"up" \| "down" \| "flat"` |  | Which way it has moved; the caption then carries an arrow and the direction as a word. |
| `help` | `ReactNode` |  | Support text, at most 35 words: what the figure counts. On a plain tile it sits behind the title as a help term; on a tile that opens its records it is an ⓘ beside the number instead, because a focusable term cannot live inside the button that opens them. |
| `helpLabel` | `string` |  | The figure's name as plain words, when `title` is not a string: the ⓘ's name and the help sheet's title. |
| `onOpen` | `() => void` |  | Opens the records behind the number (the report model). Without it the tile is plain. |
| `opensOn` | `"all" \| "phone"` |  | Where the tile is clickable. `all` (the default) on both; `phone` when the desktop page already shows the detail beside the tiles, so desktop gets no second way to the same thing. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |


|---|---|
| Use | The first link of a chat message, under its text; the composer's card while a message with a link is written, with Remove Preview. |
| Avoid | A link the product makes itself (a Button or a router Link); a mail's links (EmailFrame keeps them); a card for every link in a message (only the first gets one). |
| Phone | The same card, the width of its bubble: a wide picture runs across its top, a small or square one sits at its side; the whole card is the tap target. |
| Accessibility | The card is one link named by the page's title that says it opens a new tab; the picture is decorative beside the title; Remove Preview is a named button; a loading card says so. |
| Status | beta |
| Exports | `LinkCard` |
| Import | `import { LinkCard } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/display/LinkCard.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/display/LinkCard.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/display/LinkCard.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/LinkCard`) |

**LinkCard** props (`LinkCardProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `string` | yes | Where the card opens: the link as posted. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The page's title. |
| `site` | `string` |  | The site, as the page names itself, else its host. |
| `description` | `string \| null` |  | A line of the page's description, when it has one. |
| `image` | `string \| null` |  | The page's picture, ready to draw (fetched with the session); null while it loads. |
| `hasImage` | `boolean` |  | Whether the card has a picture at all, so its place is kept while it loads. |
| `imageWidth` | `number \| null` |  | The picture's width in pixels: a wide one runs across the top. |
| `imageHeight` | `number \| null` |  | The picture's height in pixels. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | The composer's card while the page is read: its shape, shimmering. |
| `onRemove` | `() => void` |  | The composer's card: a card that does not open, with Remove Preview. |
| `tone` | `"mine" \| "theirs" \| "plain"` |  | Where it sits: in the sender's own bubble, in another's, or on the page (the composer). |
| `onSeen` | `() => void` |  | Called once when the card first comes near the screen, so its picture is fetched only then. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing, width). |

```tsx
<LinkCard href="https://nfelia.com/" title="Nfelia: Fashion in Lagos" site="Nfelia" description="Shop the latest." image={src} imageWidth={1200} imageHeight={630} hasImage />
```

| | |

### ProgressBar

How far along something is: a bar with its percent, or a moving bar when the end is unknown; Meter is the thin inline bar with its figure (the merged Mini).

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | ProgressBar for work under way (an import, an upload, onboarding steps); Meter for a measure against a whole in a row or a card (leave used, a target met). |

| Phone | Full width; the figure stays on the same line. |
| Accessibility | ProgressBar is a progressbar with its value (or busy, with no value, while indeterminate); Meter is a meter. Both need a name: the visible label, or the name prop. Under reduced motion the indeterminate bar does not move. |

| Exports | `ProgressBar`, `Meter` |
| Import | `import { ProgressBar, Meter } from "@mycity/ui";` |

| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The visible label above the bar, Title Case (Importing Employees); also its accessible name. |

| `tone` | `"primary" \| "ok" \| "warn" \| "err" \| "info" \| "neutral" \| "chart-1" \| "chart-2" \| "chart-3" \| "chart-4"` |  | The fill colour; primary unless set. |

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

### Skeleton

## Navigation

### Chips

A row of filter chips above a list, each with an optional count: one chosen (single select) or several switched on (toggle).

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Narrowing a list by a status or a group (Everyone, Late 4, Remote 2); a board's stage switcher on a phone (F19); picking several departments with `selected`. |
| Avoid | Switching between views (use SegmentedControl or Tabs); a choice inside a form (use ChoiceField or CheckboxField); a status shown on a record (use Pill). |
| Phone | One row that scrolls sideways inside itself, never the page; each chip is a 44 px target. |
| Accessibility | A group named by `label`; each chip is a button with aria-pressed, so a screen reader hears which are on. The count is read with the label (Late 4). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Chips` |
| Import | `import { Chips } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/navigation/Chips.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/navigation/Chips.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/navigation/Chips.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Chips`) |

**Chips** props (`ChipsProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | `ReadonlyArray<Choice<V>>` | yes | The merged tuple ["late", "Late"], or { value, label, count, icon, disabled }. Labels Title Case, at most 3 words; counts as numbers. |
| `value` | `V` |  | Single select: the chip that is on. |
| `onChange` | `(value: V) => void` |  | Single select: called with the chip pressed. |
| `selected` | `readonly V[]` |  | Toggle: the chips that are on (several may be). Using it switches the row to toggle mode. |
| `onSelectedChange` | `(selected: V[]) => void` |  | Toggle: called with the new set after a chip is switched on or off. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Names the row for assistive technology ("Status", "Departments"). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing); the row keeps the merged 12 px gap below it unless overridden. |

```tsx
<Chips label="Status" value={status} onChange={setStatus} options={[["all", "Everyone"], { value: "late", label: "Late", count: 4 }]} />
<Chips label="Departments" selected={depts} onSelectedChange={setDepts} options={departments.map((d) => [d.name, d.name])} />
```

### SegmentedControl

Two to five views of the same thing side by side in one pill (Mine, My Team; Week, Month), one of them on.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Switching what a list, board or chart shows, in a toolbar or a page header; at most 5 options, each at most 3 words. |
| Avoid | A choice inside a form (use ChoiceField); filtering a list by status with counts (use Chips); the module's views (use Tabs); more than 5 options (use a select or Tabs). |
| Phone | Fills the width with equal segments, each a 44 px target; a long set scrolls sideways inside itself, never the page. |
| Accessibility | A radiogroup named by `label`, each segment a radio: one Tab stop, the arrow keys move and choose, Home and End go to the ends. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `SegmentedControl` |
| Import | `import { SegmentedControl } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/navigation/SegmentedControl.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/navigation/SegmentedControl.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/navigation/SegmentedControl.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/SegmentedControl`) |

**SegmentedControl** props (`SegmentedControlProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `V` | yes | The view showing. |
| `onChange` | `(value: V) => void` | yes | Called with the chosen view. |
| `options` | `ReadonlyArray<Choice<V>>` | yes | Two to five options: the merged tuple ["team", "My Team"], or { value, label, icon, count, disabled }. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Names the group for assistive technology ("Whose Tasks"); give one unless a visible label sits beside it. |
| `disabled` | `readonly V[]` |  | Values shown but not choosable (the merged Seg's `disabled`). |
| `small` | `boolean` |  | The 28 px desktop size for a dense toolbar (still 44 px on a phone). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<SegmentedControl label="Whose Tasks" value={scope} onChange={setScope} options={[["mine", "Mine"], ["team", "My Team"]]} />
```

### Tabs

The module's tab strip: one row of tabs under the page header, one of them active, with an optional count on each.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Sibling views of one module or record (Register, Field Assignments, Location Requests). Controlled by value, so the router drives it from ?tab=; give each tab an href so it opens in a new tab and survives a reload. |
| Avoid | Two or three views of one list in a toolbar (use SegmentedControl); filtering a list (use Chips); steps of a form (use Wizard); more than one strip on a screen. |
| Phone | One row that scrolls sideways inside itself, never the page; the active tab is brought into view; each tab is a 44 px target. On a desktop too narrow for every tab, the row keeps the tabs that fit, the active one always among them, and the rest wait behind More Tabs (a ⋯ menu at the end, dotted when a hidden tab has a count). |
| Accessibility | A tablist named by `label` (Radix underneath): one Tab stop for the strip, Left and Right between tabs, Home and End to the ends, Enter or Space activates (manual activation, so arrowing does not load every view). With TabPanel children each tab controls its panel; as a bare strip over a routed screen it controls nothing. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Tabs`, `TabPanel` |
| Import | `import { Tabs, TabPanel } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/navigation/Tabs.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/navigation/Tabs.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/navigation/Tabs.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Tabs`) |

**Tabs** props (`TabsProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `TabItem[]` | yes | The tabs, in order. |
| `value` | `string` | yes | The active tab's value (controlled: the router or the screen owns it). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the chosen tab's value; navigate or set state here. |
| `label` | `string` | yes | Names the strip for assistive technology: the module or record ("Attendance"). |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | TabPanel elements, when the views live on this screen; leave out when the router renders the view. |
| `activation` | `"manual" \| "automatic"` |  | `manual` (the default): arrows move focus and Enter activates. `automatic`: arrows activate. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes for the whole block (spacing). |

**TabPanel** props (`TabPanelProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `string` | yes | The tab it belongs to. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The view. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes (spacing). |

```tsx
<Tabs label="Attendance" value={tab} onValueChange={(t) => navigate(`/attendance?tab=${t}`)} items={[{ value: "register", label: "Register", href: "/attendance?tab=register" }]} />
<Tabs label="Employee" value={tab} onValueChange={setTab} items={items}><TabPanel value="profile">...</TabPanel></Tabs>
```

## Overlays

### ConfirmDialog

A yes or no before an action that cannot be taken back, named for the thing it acts on ("Delete Rule").

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Deleting, cancelling, revoking, emptying a folder: `if (!(await confirm({ title: "Delete Rule", destructive: true }))) return;`. The component form when a screen keeps its own state. |
| Avoid | Asking before something that can be undone (do it, and offer Undo in the toast); window.confirm (gate 16); a form (use Modal). |
| Phone | A short bottom sheet; the confirm button full width at the bottom, Cancel above it. |
| Accessibility | An alertdialog: Cancel has focus when it opens, Esc and the close button answer no. A destructive confirmation cannot be dismissed by a stray tap on the scrim. While an async confirm runs, Cancel, Esc and the close button wait (F26). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `ConfirmDialog` |
| Import | `import { ConfirmDialog } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/overlay/ConfirmDialog.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/overlay/ConfirmDialog.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/overlay/ConfirmDialog.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/ConfirmDialog`) |

**ConfirmDialog** props (`ConfirmDialogProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | yes | Whether it is showing. |
| `title` | `string` | yes | The action and the thing, Verb Noun, at most 4 words: "Delete Rule", "Empty Trash". |
| `body` | `ReactNode` |  | At most one sentence of 20 words on what follows, only when the title does not say it. |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` |  | The confirm button, Verb Noun; the title by default. |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` |  | The way out. Default "Cancel". |
| `destructive` | `boolean` |  | A red confirm button, and the scrim no longer dismisses. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` |  | Whether Esc and the scrim answer no. Default: true unless destructive. |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void \| Promise<unknown>` | yes | Called on confirm. A promise keeps the button busy until it settles. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | yes | Called on Cancel, Esc, the close button, or (when dismissible) the scrim. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | Where it mounts; document.body by default. |

```tsx
const confirm = useConfirm(); if (await confirm({ title: "Delete Rule", destructive: true })) remove(rule);
<ConfirmDialog open={open} title="Revoke Device" destructive onConfirm={revoke} onCancel={() => setOpen(false)} />
```

### LockScreen

The full-screen lock over the staff app when a session ends: who is signed in, why it locked, and their password to carry on.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | The staff app's session lock only (the time limit, the idle limit, a session ended elsewhere). The work underneath stays exactly as it was. |
| Avoid | Any other prompt (use Modal or useConfirm); the first sign-in (the sign-in screen). |
| Phone | Fills the screen the same way: the card sits in 16 px gutters and its buttons stack full width. |
| Accessibility | Radix Dialog underneath: aria-modal, focus moves to the first field and stays inside, Esc and the backdrop do nothing. It stacks over any dialog already open. The title names it; the reason is its description. |
| Status | beta |
| Exports | `LockScreen` |
| Import | `import { LockScreen } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/overlay/LockScreen.tsx` |

| `photo` | `string \| null` |  | Their photo, if they have one; the initials otherwise. |

### Menu

A short list of actions behind one button (the ⋮ on a record, the + in a composer, the account menu).

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Secondary actions on a record or a row, choices behind a split button (Schedule). Items are Verb Noun; destructive ones are red and come last. |
| Avoid | The main action (a Button of its own); choosing a value in a form (SelectField); navigation between pages (links); more than about 8 items. |
| Phone | An action sheet from the bottom: large rows, destructive items in red, Cancel at the foot. |
| Accessibility | Radix menu on desktop: arrow keys move, Enter chooses, typing jumps to an item, Esc closes and focus returns to the button. The button needs a name (an IconButton label). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Menu` |
| Import | `import { Menu } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Menu.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Menu.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Menu.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Menu`) |

**Menu** props (`MenuProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `((props: MenuTriggerProps) => ReactNode) \| ReactElement` | yes | The button that opens it: a function that spreads the props it is given onto a button, or the button itself. |
| `items` | `MenuItem[]` | yes | The actions, top to bottom; "sep" draws a divider. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "end"` |  | Which edge of the button the menu lines up with on desktop. Default `end`. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Names the action sheet on a phone for screen readers. Default "Actions". |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | Where it mounts; document.body by default. |

```tsx
<Menu trigger={(p) => <IconButton {...p} icon="dots" label="More Actions" />} items={[{ label: "Archive", icon: "book", onSelect: archive }, "sep", { label: "Move to Trash", icon: "x", danger: true, onSelect: trash }]} />
```

### Modal

THE modal: a centred dialog on desktop and a bottom sheet on a phone, opened with useModal or controlled with open.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Create or edit with up to 6 fields, a record's detail, a short reader. useModal().open({ title, body }) from anywhere under ModalProvider; <Modal open> when the screen owns the state. |
| Avoid | A destructive yes or no (use useConfirm); editing the record behind it on desktop (use SidePanel); more than 6 fields (a wizard); a stack of dialogs (opening one replaces the last). |
| Phone | A bottom sheet that drags down to close, with the main action full width at the bottom; `full` makes it a full-screen sheet (a composer, a long form). It stays above the keyboard, header in view; once it holds a text field only the close button, Cancel or Esc close it. |
| Accessibility | Radix Dialog underneath: aria-modal, focus moves in and is trapped, Esc closes, focus returns to the opener. The title (at most 4 words) names it. With unsaved changes, Esc, the scrim, the close button or a drag ask once to discard. Its buttons are one ActionGroup: while one is working the others wait, and Esc, the scrim, a drag and the close button do nothing until it finishes (F26). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Modal`, `ModalProvider`, `ModalFooter`, `Grow` |
| Import | `import { Modal, ModalProvider, ModalFooter, Grow } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Modal.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Modal.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Modal.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Modal`) |

**Modal** props (`ModalProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | yes | Whether it is showing. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | yes | Called to close it: after a dismissal (Esc, scrim, close button, drag), once any unsaved changes are discarded. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes | The title: a noun phrase of at most 4 words, Title Case ("New Rule", "Edit Worksite"). |
| `sub` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the title, at most 8 words, desktop only; kept as the dialog's description. |
| `children` | `ModalContent` |  | The body, or a function of `close`. |
| `footer` | `ModalContent` |  | Footer buttons only (Cancel, then the primary), or a function of `close`. A body can also use ModalFooter. |
| `wide` | `boolean` |  | The wider desktop dialog (tables, documents). Same as size="wide". |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "wide"` |  | Desktop width: `sm` a confirmation, `md` a form (the default), `wide` a table or document. |
| `full` | `boolean` |  | A full-screen sheet on a phone (a composer, a long form, a reader). No change on desktop. |
| `side` | `boolean` |  | A side panel over the record on desktop instead of a centred dialog; a full sheet on a phone. SidePanel sets it. |
| `dirty` | `boolean` |  | Unsaved changes: a dismissal asks once to discard them. Forms inside can also say so with useUnsavedChanges. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` |  | false: Esc, the scrim and a drag do nothing; the close button and the footer still close it. Default true. |
| `blur` | `boolean` |  | Blur the screen behind the scrim, for a prompt that must be answered before anything else (the clock prompts). |
| `role` | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog"` |  | `alertdialog` for a confirmation that must be answered. Default `dialog`. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | Where it mounts; document.body by default (the gallery passes its themed frame). |
| `bodyClassName` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the scrolling body. |

**ModalProvider** props (`ModalProviderProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes | The app. |
| `resetKey` | `unknown` |  | Whatever is open closes when this changes: the app passes its route, so a new screen never inherits a dialog. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | Where the modals mount; document.body by default. |

**ModalFooter** props (`ModalFooterProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes | Buttons only: Cancel first, the primary last (it lands full width at the bottom on a phone). |

**Grow** props (`GrowProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes. |

```tsx
modal.open({ title: "New Rule", body: (close) => <RuleForm close={close} /> })
<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Edit Worksite" footer={<Button variant="primary">Save Worksite</Button>}>{fields}</Modal>
```

### PhonePage

A full-screen page that slides in from the right over the screen on a phone, like a native app's next screen: Back, a title, its own actions, a body that scrolls.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A place a person goes into and comes back from without leaving the screen they were on: the notification pane, Notification Settings over it. |
| Avoid | A form or a record on desktop (use Modal or SidePanel); a short choice (use Sheet); a real screen with its own address (a route). |
| Phone | This is its phone form: the whole screen, under the status bar and above the home bar, swiped right or Back to close. On desktop it draws the same page as a panel on the right. |
| Accessibility | A modal dialog named by `title` (Radix underneath, through Vaul): focus moves in and is trapped, Esc and Back close it, focus returns to the opener. Back is a named button; `actions` are IconButtons with labels. |
| Status | beta |
| Exports | `PhonePage` |
| Import | `import { PhonePage } from "@mycity/ui";` |

| Test | `packages/ui/src/overlay/PhonePage.test.tsx` |

| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes | The page's title, at most 3 words, Title Case. |

| `bodyRef` | `(el: HTMLDivElement \| null) => void` |  | Called with the scrolling body, for a list that loads more near its end or pulls to refresh. |

```tsx
<PhonePage open={open} onClose={close} title="Notifications" actions={<IconButton icon="cog" label="Notification Settings" />}>{rows}</PhonePage>
```

### Popover

A small panel anchored to the button that opens it: filters, a quick pick, a short preview.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A few controls that belong to one button (Filters, Columns, a date preset list), a preview that needs no page. |
| Avoid | A list of actions (use Menu); a form that saves (use Modal); help text (use HelpTerm, which has its own popover). |
| Phone | A bottom sheet titled by `title`, opened by a tap on the same button. |
| Accessibility | A non-modal dialog named by `title`: focus moves in, Esc or a click outside closes it, focus returns to the button. The button says it has a popup and whether it is open. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Popover` |
| Import | `import { Popover } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Popover.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Popover.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Popover.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Popover`) |

**Popover** props (`PopoverProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `ReactElement` | yes | The button that opens it: one element that takes a ref. |
| `title` | `string` | yes | Names the popover, at most 4 words: the sheet's title on a phone and the accessible name on desktop. |
| `children` | `ReactNode \| ((close: () => void) => ReactNode)` | yes | The panel's content, or a function of `close`. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Leave both unset to let the popover keep its own. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when it opens or closes. |
| `side` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` |  | Which side of the button on desktop. Default `bottom`. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` |  | Alignment along that side. Default `start`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Extra classes for the desktop panel (a width from the scale, such as w-80). |

```tsx
<Popover title="Filter Leave" trigger={<Button icon="flag">Filters</Button>}>{filters}</Popover>
```

### Sheet

The phone's bottom sheet: slides up with a spring, closes by dragging down, a tap on the scrim or Esc; one with a text field closes only on purpose.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Underneath Modal, SidePanel, Popover and Menu on a phone; directly for a phone-only sheet (the More launcher, a KPI detail). |
| Avoid | A dialog on desktop (use Modal, which is this sheet on a phone and a centred dialog on desktop); a toast or banner for news. |
| Phone | This is the phone form. `full` fills the screen for a long form or a reader; otherwise it is as tall as its content, up to most of the screen, with a grab handle. With the keyboard up it stays above it, header in view. Once it holds a text field it has no handle and a drag or a scrim tap never closes it (a scrim tap puts the keyboard away); the close button, Cancel and Esc do. |
| Accessibility | A modal dialog (Radix underneath): focus moves in and is trapped, Esc closes, focus returns to the opener. The title names it; `hideHeader` keeps the title for screen readers only. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Sheet` |
| Import | `import { Sheet } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Sheet.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Sheet.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/overlay/Sheet.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Sheet`) |

**Sheet** props (`SheetProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | `boolean` | yes | Whether the sheet is showing. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | yes | Called when the person dismisses it (drag down, scrim, Esc, the close button). Keep `open` true to refuse, and the sheet springs back. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes | The heading, at most 4 words, Title Case. |
| `sub` | `ReactNode` |  | A short line under the heading; hidden on a phone, kept as the dialog's description. |
| `hideHeader` | `boolean` |  | No header row: the title is read by screen readers only (an action sheet). |
| `full` | `boolean` |  | Fill the screen (a long form, a composer, a reader) instead of fitting the content. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons for the footer; the main action is last and full width at the bottom. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The body. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` |  | false: drag, scrim and Esc do nothing (the close button and Cancel still work). Default true. A sheet holding a text field ignores the drag and the scrim anyway. |
| `blur` | `boolean` |  | Blur the screen behind the scrim, for a prompt that must be answered before anything else (the clock prompts). |
| `role` | `"dialog" \| "alertdialog"` |  | `alertdialog` for a confirmation. Default `dialog`. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | Where the sheet mounts; document.body by default (the gallery passes its themed frame). |


### Tooltip

A small label that appears beside a control on hover or keyboard focus, desktop only.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A truncated name in full, the words behind an icon-only control that is not an IconButton (IconButton draws its own from its label). Every hover label in the product: never the browser's title attribute (gate 21). |
| Avoid | Help or explanation (use HelpTerm); anything a person must read to act; anything on a phone, where there is no hover. |
| Phone | Nothing: the child renders alone, since a touch screen has no hover and the control already carries its name. |
| Accessibility | Opens on hover after a short pause and at once on keyboard focus; Esc closes it; the text is announced as the control's description. The control keeps its own accessible name. It passes a ref and props through to its child, so it can sit inside a Menu or Dialog trigger. Never the browser's own title tooltip (gate 21). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Tooltip` |

## Help

### Details

One row at the foot of a card, a chevron and the word Details, that opens a short section of support facts.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Tier 2 facts a person needs now and then to act on the card above it: the rules a figure counts, a schedule's grace period, a policy line. Short label and value pairs rather than prose, at most 60 words. |
| Avoid | One or two sentences about one word (use HelpTerm); how the system works or why it was built (tier 3: the manual); more than one per card; anything a person needs every visit (show it open). |
| Phone | A 44 px row that opens the body in a bottom sheet, closed by dragging down. |
| Accessibility | A button with aria-expanded that controls the body (desktop) or says it opens a dialog (phone). Closed on every visit: the open state is never remembered. The body (data-ui="details") stays in the DOM, hidden, so the word limit can be checked. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Details` |
| Import | `import { Details } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/help/Details.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/help/Details.test.tsx` |

**Details** props (`DetailsProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `Array<[ReactNode, ReactNode]>` |  | Short label and value pairs, Title Case labels ("Grace Period", "10 minutes"). Preferred over prose. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Free content, after the pairs, when pairs do not fit: one or two short lines. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The phone sheet's title, at most 4 words. Default "Details". |


### HelpTerm

The word a piece of help explains, with a light dotted underline; hovering, tabbing to or tapping it shows one or two sentences.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Tier 2 support text of one or two sentences attached to the word it explains: a field label, a KPI title, a column header, a card title ("Over By", "Grace Period"). |
| Avoid | Anything a person must read before acting (put it on the control or in the confirmation); more than 35 words (tier 3: the manual); a section of facts (use Details); a chart or icon with no word (use InfoButton). |
| Phone | No hover: a tap opens the text in a bottom sheet titled by the term, closed by dragging down, the scrim or Esc. |
| Accessibility | The term is a button with a dotted underline. The text is always in the DOM in a visually hidden node outside any label or heading, linked with aria-describedby, so it never joins the accessible name of what it explains. Desktop: opens after about 300 ms on hover or on reaching it with Tab, stays while the pointer is over the term or the popover, Esc closes it (WCAG 1.4.13). Pass helpId to describe a field's control by the same text. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `HelpTerm` |
| Import | `import { HelpTerm } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/help/HelpTerm.tsx` |

| `help` | `ReactNode` | yes | The help: one or two sentences, at most 35 words, sentence case. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The phone sheet's title; the term itself when it is plain text, else "Help". |

| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` |  | The popover's alignment along that side. Default `center`. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` |  | Where the popover and the sheet mount; document.body by default (the gallery passes its themed frame). |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only. |

## Feedback

### ErrorBoundary

Catches a crash in one screen so the rest of the app keeps working, and shows ErrorState with Try Again in its place.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Around each screen in the shell, keyed by module and tab so moving to another screen starts it fresh; around a lazily loaded heavy part (a chart, the editor). |
| Avoid | Catching a failed request (useApi gives its error to ErrorState); wrapping every small component; hiding a bug that should be fixed. |
| Phone | The same ErrorState, its Try Again full width. |
| Accessibility | The fallback is role="alert"; the rail, the tabs and the back button stay usable. Try Again renders the children again. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `ErrorBoundary` |
| Import | `import { ErrorBoundary } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/feedback/ErrorBoundary.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/feedback/ErrorBoundary.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/feedback/ErrorBoundary.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/ErrorBoundary`) |

**ErrorBoundary** props (`ErrorBoundaryProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What it guards: a screen, or a heavy part of one. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode \| ((error: Error, reset: () => void) => ReactNode)` |  | What shows instead; a function gets the error and a reset. Default: ErrorState, "This screen hit a problem", Try Again. |
| `onError` | `(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo) => void` |  | Told of each crash (to report it); the console always gets it too. |
| `resetKeys` | `readonly unknown[]` |  | When any of these change while the fallback shows, the children render again (a route, a record id). |

```tsx
<ErrorBoundary key={`${module}:${tab}`}><Screen /></ErrorBoundary>
<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => <ErrorState message="The chart did not draw" onRetry={reset} />}>{chart}</ErrorBoundary>
```

### ErrorState

Something did not load: one line saying so, and Try Again.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | In place of a list, a card's content or a screen whose request failed (pass the ApiError and the reload); the fallback of ErrorBoundary. |
| Avoid | A failed save (use toast.error, or the field's own mark); an empty result (use EmptyState); a stack trace, an error code or an apology paragraph. |
| Phone | Centred; Try Again is full width within thumb reach. |
| Accessibility | role="alert", so the line is announced when it replaces the content. Try Again is a real button; it is left out where trying again cannot help (no access, not found). The server's reference, when there is one, is shown for support as data. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `ErrorState` |
| Import | `import { ErrorState } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/feedback/ErrorState.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/feedback/ErrorState.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/feedback/ErrorState.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/ErrorState`) |

**ErrorState** props (`ErrorStateProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `error` | `ErrorLike \| null` |  | The failure: the ApiError of the request (useApi's or usePaged's `error`). |
| `message` | `ReactNode` |  | The line, when the status does not say enough (sentence case, at most 8 words). |
| `onRetry` | `() => void` |  | Reloads what failed; shows Try Again. |
| `page` | `boolean` |  | A whole screen failed: the error drawing instead of the glyph, with more room. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<ErrorState error={list.error} onRetry={list.reload} />
<ErrorState page message="This screen hit a problem" onRetry={reset} />
```

|---|---|

| Accessibility | Shown in a polite live region named New Notifications, so it is read without moving focus; the banner is one button named by its title and text, with a named Dismiss button. It stays while hovered or touched, and fades only when motion is allowed. |
| Status | beta |

## Forms

### AddressField

An address typed with suggestions from our own address search; picking one fills the address and hands back its coordinates.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Any address in a form: a worksite, a field site, a client visit, a home. Pass `onPick` where the place's latitude and longitude fill the form's own fields. |
| Avoid | Calling the provider from the browser (the key stays on the server); a search box that only finds (PlaceSearch); the browser's own autofill list or a `<datalist>` (gate 21). |
| Phone | 44 px tall with 16 px text; the suggestions open under the field as 44 px rows, inside the sheet's own scroll. |

### CardPicker

The cards a person puts on a KPI row: tick up to four, keep them in order with Move Up and Move Down, the cards their role fixes locked and first.

| Use | Choose Cards on Home, and a role's cards on Settings: inside a Modal whose footer holds Cancel, any reset and the save. |

Move Up and Move Down are worded buttons named for their card, unavailable (not removed) at either end, and focus stays with a card as it moves. A polite status reads the count after a tick, a card's new place after a move, and the limit when a pick is refused; the refused tick is marked invalid and described by the error. |
| Status | beta |
| Exports | `CardPicker` |
| Import | `import { CardPicker } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/form/CardPicker.tsx` |

### Field

### Form

The one <form>: Enter submits, the browser's own bubbles are off, and a save it is waiting on cannot be sent twice; with FormFooter, the buttons at its foot.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Around every set of fields; onSubmit comes from the form hook (form.submit(save) or a handler that calls form.check()). Return the save's promise and the form refuses another submit until it settles, its submit button spins and its other buttons wait (F26). |
| Avoid | A <form> written anywhere else (gate 12); text in a footer (buttons only); a disabled submit button. |

| Accessibility | A real form element, so Enter submits and assistive technology announces it; FormFooter keeps the primary last in the tab order. While a save runs the submit button says aria-busy and stays focusable. |

The upload engine: the only file input in the product, with a percentage per file and the vault's document as its answer.

| Use | Anywhere a person attaches a file: a CV, a receipt, a signed offer, a mail attachment, an import sheet. |

| Phone | The drop zone is a full-width tap target, since a phone cannot drop; every file shows its own percentage as it travels. |
| Accessibility | The words in the drop zone are a real button, which opens the picker; the progress is a named meter per file, and each file's state is in words as well as a glyph. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `UploadField` |
| Import | `import { UploadField } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/form/UploadField.tsx` |

## Data

### Calendar

A month at a glance, Monday first, with what happens on each day.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Leave across a month, a shift pattern, interviews, a payroll calendar, anything a person reads by date. |
| Avoid | A list of dated records (use DataView); a date to type into a form (use DateField); more than three events on one day without opening it. |
| Phone | The same seven columns at a shorter height; a day's events are one tap each, and the page never scrolls sideways. |
| Accessibility | A table of weeks with the weekdays as real headers, so a screen reader can say "Wednesday 14"; Sundays are marked in words, not only by their shade. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Calendar` |
| Import | `import { Calendar } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/data/Calendar.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/data/Calendar.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/data/Calendar.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Calendar`) |

**Calendar** props (`CalendarProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `year` | `number` | yes | The year. |
| `month` | `number` | yes | The month, 0 for January, as `Date` counts them. |
| `events` | `CalendarEvent[]` | yes | Everything happening that month; days outside it are ignored. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | What sits at the right of the title row (the month's own controls); the time zone otherwise. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<Calendar year={2026} month={9} events={[{ date: "2026-10-14", label: "Ada on leave" }]} />
```

### DataView

THE shared list: a dense table on desktop and a card list on a phone from the same rows, with the pager, server sort, selection, bulk actions and Export.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Every list of records a person reads or acts on: employees, leave requests, expenses, candidates, partners. |
| Avoid | A second table of your own; sorting or filtering the 25 rows on screen; a column chooser; a visible table on a phone. |
| Phone | The columns become cards: the first value is the card's title, the next three are label and value pairs, and sort moves into an action sheet. There is never a <table> (gate 11). |
| Accessibility | The table has a caption, sortable headers carry aria-sort and are buttons, a clickable row is reachable by Tab and Enter, and a reloading list says aria-busy. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `DataView`, `LoadingRows` |
| Import | `import { DataView, LoadingRows } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/data/DataView.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/data/DataView.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/data/DataView.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/DataView`) |

**DataView** props (`DataViewProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | `DataViewColumn<R>[]` | yes | The columns, left to right. The first is the card's title on a phone. |
| `rowKey` | `(row: R) => string` | yes | Names one row for the key, the pager's count and screen readers. |
| `list` | `DataViewList<R>` |  | A server-paged list (a `usePaged()` result): the rows, the page, the search, the sort and the state in one. Pass this or `rows`. |
| `rows` | `R[]` |  | A set already in hand (a record's own steps, a sheet's rows). Pass this or `list`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | A request is in flight, for a set passed as `rows`. |
| `error` | `ApiError \| null` |  | The read's error, for a set passed as `rows`. |
| `page` | `PageMeta` |  | The server's page, for a set passed as `rows`; the pager is drawn when `onPage` comes with it. |
| `onPage` | `(n: number) => void` |  | Asks for a page number, for a set passed as `rows`. |
| `onReload` | `() => void` |  | Asks for the rows again, behind Try Again, for a set passed as `rows`. |
| `caption` | `string` |  | Names the table for screen readers; the title unless set. Required when there is no title. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | The card's title above the list, at most 4 words. |
| `help` | `ReactNode` |  | Support text behind the title, at most 35 words. |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | What sits at the right of the title row: a button, a menu, a pill. |
| `right` | `ReactNode` |  | The merged name for `actions`; kept so screens move by an import change. |
| `search` | `string` |  | A search box above the list, with this as its placeholder (at most 3 words). Needs `list.setQ`. |
| `onRowClick` | `(row: R) => void` |  | Opens a row. A phone card becomes one tap target; a desktop row is reachable by Tab. |
| `selectedKey` | `string \| null` |  | The row drawn as the one being looked at (a desktop list beside a panel). |
| `selection` | `DataViewSelection` |  | Row selection and its bulk actions. |
| `onExport` | `() => Promise<unknown>` |  | Makes the whole filtered list into a file on the server and saves it on this device (ExportButton). |
| `noun` | `string` |  | What one row is, for the pager's count ("employee"). |
| `nounPlural` | `string` |  | The plural, when it is not the noun with an s. |
| `empty` | `{ title: ReactNode; text?: ReactNode; icon?: IconName }` |  | What to show when there are no rows. |
| `wide` | `boolean` |  | A wide table scrolls inside its own card rather than squeezing its columns. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Anything under the pager. |
| `bare` | `boolean` |  | Draw it without its card, inside one that is already there. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

**LoadingRows** props (`LoadingRowsProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | `number` |  | How many lines to draw; 4 unless set. |

```tsx
<DataView list={list} columns={columns} rowKey={(r) => r.employee_id} caption="Employees" noun="employee" search="Search People" />
<DataView rows={rows} loading={read.loading} error={read.error} columns={columns} rowKey={(r) => r.id} caption="Approval Steps" bare />
```

### ExportButton

Asks the server for the whole filtered list as a file and saves it on the device that pressed, once the worker has made it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Beside a list that a person needs outside the product (a payroll run, an attendance month, an expense claim set). |
| Avoid | Building a file in the browser from the 25 rows on screen; sending the file anywhere but the device that pressed. |
| Phone | The same button, full width in the toolbar; the file goes to Downloads, or the share sheet on an iPhone app. |
| Accessibility | Busy until the file is saved, and the button stays pressable rather than disabled (FRONTEND_GUIDE §9.4). |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `ExportButton` |
| Import | `import { ExportButton } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/data/ExportButton.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/data/ExportButton.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/data/ExportButton.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/ExportButton`) |

**ExportButton** props (`ExportButtonProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onExport` | `() => Promise<unknown>` | yes | Makes the file of the list's CURRENT filters, which the caller holds, and saves it on this device: it asks the server for the whole filtered list, never the page on screen, waits for the file and saves it. Resolves once it is saved; resolving `false` means nothing was saved and the person has already been told why, so no toast says otherwise. |
| `children` | `string` |  | The label: Verb Noun, at most 3 words. "Export" unless set. |
| `message` | `string` |  | What the toast says once the file is saved. At most 8 words. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<ExportButton onExport={() => saveExport(api.call("POST /api/v1/audit/exports", { body: filters }))} />
```

### Kanban

A board of stages: columns of cards on desktop, and on a phone a stage switcher over the cards of one stage (F19).

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | A pipeline a person moves records along: partnerships, recruitment, tasks, requisitions. |
| Avoid | A list that is not staged (use DataView); dragging as the only way to move a card; more than six stages. |
| Phone | No dragging at all (F19): chips with counts choose the stage, and a card's Move To opens the other stages as an action sheet. |
| Accessibility | Each column is a named group; Move To is a real menu, so a card can be moved by keyboard and by screen reader, never only by dragging. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Kanban`, `KanbanCardBody` |
| Import | `import { Kanban, KanbanCardBody } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/data/Kanban.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/data/Kanban.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/data/Kanban.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Kanban`) |

**Kanban** props (`KanbanProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `columns` | `KanbanColumn[]` | yes | The stages, left to right. |
| `onOpen` | `(card: string, column: string) => void` |  | Opens a card's record. |
| `onMove` | `(card: string, from: string, to: string) => void` |  | Moves a card to another stage. Without it the board is read only. On desktop a card can also be dragged; Move To exists either way, because a keyboard and a phone cannot drag (F19). |

### Pager

Page controls under a list, showing the server's true total ("312 employees") and Previous and Next.

| | |
|---|---|
| Use | Under any server-paged list: DataView draws one for you, and a card grid or a picker that pages itself takes one directly. |
| Avoid | A page-size chooser, a jump-to-page box, or "showing 25 of many"; the size is the server's 25 and is never offered. |
| Phone | The count sits above the buttons, which are full width and 44 px, so paging is a thumb reach. |
| Accessibility | A navigation landmark named for the list it pages, so two lists on one screen stay apart; the count is a live region, so a screen reader hears the new range after Next. |
| Status | stable |
| Exports | `Pager` |
| Import | `import { Pager } from "@mycity/ui";` |
| File | `packages/ui/src/data/Pager.tsx` |
| Test | `packages/ui/src/data/Pager.test.tsx` |
| Gallery | `packages/ui/src/data/Pager.gallery.tsx` (`npm run gallery`, `#/Pager`) |

**Pager** props (`PagerProps`)

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `PageMeta \| undefined \| null` | yes | The `page` object from the list response; nothing is drawn without it. |
| `onPage` | `(number: number) => void` | yes | Asks for a page number. |
| `noun` | `string` |  | What one row is, lower case ("employee"); "record" unless set. |
| `nounPlural` | `string` |  | The plural, when it is not the noun with an s ("people", "queries"). |
| `label` | `string` |  | The list these pages belong to ("Annual Goals"), which names the landmark; the noun unless set. Two lists on one screen each need their own. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout classes only (spacing). |

```tsx
<Pager page={list.page} onPage={list.setPage} noun="employee" />
```

### Toolbar

The row of controls above a list: its search box, filter selects and actions, wrapping on a narrow screen.

| | |
|---|---|

| Avoid | Page-level actions (they belong in PageHeader); a column chooser; more than four filters on one list. |
| Phone | The controls stack full width in the order given, so the search box is first under the thumb; each is 44 px. |
| Accessibility | A group named for the list it controls, so a screen reader can skip past the filters to the rows. |
